2	name: gravity-ui
3	description: Builds, fixes, styles, and composes UI with the Gravity UI design system — the React ecosystem of @gravity-ui/* packages (uikit, charts, table, navigation, date-components, icons, and more). Routes to the correct package when look-alikes exist, applies theming and required setup, and prevents invented component APIs. Applies when working with @gravity-ui imports, uikit, ThemeProvider, --g- CSS tokens, or any prompt (EN or RU) mentioning gravity-ui, гравити, дизайн-система, компоненты, дашборд, таблица, график, or форма. Also installs required specialized Gravity UI packages when they are absent.
4	---
5	
6	# Building UI with Gravity UI
7	
8	Build UI on **real** Gravity UI components, not from memory. Gravity UI is a
9	multi-package React design system (`@gravity-ui/*`), so the two things that go
10	wrong are picking the wrong package and using an API from the wrong version.
11	This skill routes you to the right package, grounds you in the installed
12	version, and stops you from inventing APIs — match the installed versions and
13	follow the ecosystem catalog instead of guessing.
14	
15	## Efficiency guardrails
16	
17	- Do not read the same file twice. Reuse evidence already present in the session.
18	- Do not dump a reference file wholesale. Use targeted `rg -n -C 4` searches and keep each result below
19	  200 lines unless the whole file is necessary to resolve the task.
20	- Batch package, component, and symbol lookups into as few commands as possible.
21	- Stop documentation research as soon as package choice, import path, required setup, and uncertain props
22	  are confirmed. Documentation is evidence for decisions, not a checklist to read in full.
23	- Do not query unpkg, package source repositories, or alternative documentation mirrors.
24	- Do not install browsers or screenshot tooling, and do not start a dev server for routine verification,
25	  unless the user explicitly requests visual or browser verification.
26	- Run typecheck/build after implementation. If it fails, inspect only the failing API, fix it, and rerun
27	  the check. Do not repeatedly rebuild unchanged code.
28	
29	## Step 0 — pick the right package first (ecosystem routing)
30	
31	Before doing anything else, work out which `@gravity-ui/*` library the task
32	needs. Do not guess from training data — the ecosystem has look-alike packages
33	(`charts` vs `chartkit`, uikit `Table` vs `@gravity-ui/table`, `date-components`
34	vs `date-utils`, …) and picking the wrong one is the #1 failure.
35	Choose from the task's functionality, not only from dependencies already present in the project.
36	Open [`references/package-routing.md`](references/package-routing.md) and read
37	its top **first**: it opens with a task → package decision table that settles the
38	common cases (landing page, dashboard, data grid, calendar, charts, editor, app
39	shell, i18n), followed by the ecosystem catalog with a one-line "what it's for /
40	what to use instead" per package for everything else. Use it to choose the
41	package, then come back here for Step 1.
42	
43	Search the catalog for the task's relevant terms and read the matching package entries. Do not read the
44	entire catalog when its top and those entries are sufficient.
45	
46	Only after the package is chosen, run Step 1 to ground in that package's
47	installed version and API.
48	
49	## Step 1 — ground in the installed version of the chosen package
50	
51	1. **Read `package.json`.** Note each installed `@gravity-ui/*` package and its
52	   version. The installed version is the source of truth, not your memory.
53	   Resolve ranges from `node_modules` (`<pkg>/package.json` `version` field), not
54	   the range string in the root `package.json`.
55	
56	   If the chosen specialized package other than `@gravity-ui/uikit` is absent, add it with the project's
57	   existing package manager before importing it. Install its documented peer dependencies too, then
58	   resolve the installed version and continue with the local evidence below. Do not fall back to uikit,
59	   raw HTML, or a foreign library merely because the specialized package was initially absent. If
60	   installation is blocked, report the exact failure.
61	
62	2. **Fetch the docs for the package you are about to use, in this order,
63	   stopping at the first source that answers your question:**
64	
65	   (a) **LOCAL** — start with `node_modules/@gravity-ui/<pkg>/dist/docs/INDEX.md` or `node_modules/@gravity-ui/<pkg>/build/docs/INDEX.md`.
66	      If `INDEX.md` is absent for this package, fall back to the package's root `node_modules/@gravity-ui/<pkg>/README.md`.
67	      This is the *exact* installed version — always preferred for version-sensitive questions.
68	      Note: bundled docs are a recent addition — `uikit` ships `build/docs` only from **7.45.0**;
69	      older installs have no local docs at all, and that is expected, not an error. Go to (b).
70	      If an import, component, hook, or prop remains uncertain, inspect only its exact installed `.d.ts`
71	      before moving online. Batch all uncertain symbol lookups for that package.
72	   (b) **ONLINE** — per-package llms.txt at the **major line**:
73	      `https://gravity-ui.com/llms/<pkg>/<major>/llms.txt`
74	      (e.g. `/llms/uikit/7/llms.txt` for `^7.2.1`). The major-line URL serves the
75	      latest minor of that major — it tracks the major but not the exact patch.
76	      Use it when LOCAL has no docs for the package.
77	
78	3. **Fallback rule — never silently proceed on a failed or empty source:**
79	
80	   - If LOCAL has no README / `dist/docs` / `build/docs` for the package, or they are empty
81	     → fetch the ONLINE major-line llms.txt (b).
82	   - If the ONLINE request fails — network timeout, DNS, connection refused
83	     (air-gapped / corporate proxy), HTTP 404 (major not hosted), or an empty /
84	     non-markdown body → fall back to LOCAL README + dist/docs or build/docs (a).
85	   - **Do NOT use the `/llms/<pkg>/llms.txt` "latest" alias** as a fallback — it
86	     serves the newest major, which may differ from the installed one and have a
87	     different API. The major-line URL is the versioned fallback; below it, go
88	     LOCAL, not "latest".
89	   - If BOTH are unreachable for a package → STOP and tell the user the
90	     package's docs are unreachable. Do not guess its API from training data.
91	
92	For a bounded local inspection, run:
93	
94	```sh
95	.agents/skills/gravity-ui/scripts/inspect-package.sh uikit Button Card Switch ThemeProvider
96	```
97	
98	The script reports the resolved version, available local documentation, and declaration files matching
99	the requested symbols. Read only the returned files needed to confirm an uncertain API.
100	
101	## Step 2 — implement on the chosen packages, then typecheck
102	
103	1. **Implement using only the `@gravity-ui/*` packages chosen in Step 0 and
104	   confirmed installed in Step 1.** Import from those packages exactly — do
105	   not substitute look-alike libraries (MUI, Ant, plain `<input>`) and do not
106	   reach for a `@gravity-ui/*` package that Step 1 did not confirm installed.
107	   Follow the prop APIs from the docs you just read, not memory; if a prop
108	   you want is not documented, it does not exist — use the documented one, or
109	   ask the user.
110	
111	2. **Apply the cross-cutting rules** in `rules/hallucination-traps.md` while
112	   writing: typography variants, the flex contract, theming/ladders,
113	   `Button view`, `Icon data`. Per-component traps live in the package's own
114	   `dist/docs`.
115	
116	3. **Typecheck before declaring done.** Run the project's typecheck command
117	   (typically `tsc --noEmit`; for monorepos, the workspace's typecheck script).
118	   Fix every error before reporting completion — a type error almost always
119	   means a wrong/invented prop, a wrong import path, or a version mismatch,
120	   which is precisely what Steps 0–1 were meant to prevent.
121	
122	   - If the typecheck surfaces a prop/path that contradicts the docs you read
123	     in Step 1, trust the **installed version** (the typechecker), not the
124	     docs snapshot — the docs may be from a different minor. Re-ground: read
125	     the package's `dist/docs/INDEX.md` in `node_modules` for the exact
126	     installed types.
127	   - If the typecheck is unavailable (no TS in the project), say so
128	     explicitly and ask the user how they want to verify; do not silently
129	     skip verification.
130	   - **Escape hatch.** If the user explicitly waived verification ("just
131	     sketch it", "quick prototype", "no need to check"), you may skip the
132	     typecheck — but state this plainly in your reply: *"typecheck skipped by
133	     user request — code is not verified"*. Do not skip silently.
134	   - **Know what typecheck does not cover.** A green `tsc` proves the API is
135	     real; it says nothing about layout or contrast. Before reporting done,
136	     say so, and either check or list for the user to check by hand: the
137	     screen in both `light` and `dark` themes (text and controls on colored
138	     fills especially), narrow (~375px) and wide (~1400px) viewports for
139	     horizontal overflow, and empty / loading / error states.
140	
141	## Hard rules
142	
143	- **`@gravity-ui/uikit` MUST be installed in every Gravity UI project.** It is
144	  the base component + design-token library every other `@gravity-ui/*` package
145	  builds on; without it components render unstyled. If `package.json` lacks it,
146	  stop and have the user install and configure it first (setup:
147	  `https://gravity-ui.com/llms/uikit/llms.txt`).
148	- **Read `package.json` before importing any `@gravity-ui/*` package.** Never
149	  assume a package is installed; never assume its major version.
150	- **Do not invent props or components.** Before using a component API you are
151	  not 100% sure of, check `rules/hallucination-traps.md` (ecosystem patterns)
152	  and the component's README in `dist/docs`. If still unsure, ask the user
153	  rather than guessing.
154	- **Never guess icon names** — they are hallucinated more often than not. To
155	  match an icon from a screenshot/photo/mock, run `scripts/icon-image-search.sh`
156	  (reverse image search). With only a description, look the name up on
157	  `gravity-ui.com/icons` or ask the user — do not invent one. Then pass it as an
158	  object (`<Icon data={CheckIcon} />`), never a string key. See
159	  `references/icons.md`.
160	- **Theming uses semantic `--g-*` tokens.** Never hardcode colors (`#fff`,
161	  `blue-500`); never hand-write `dark:` overrides. Full token tables live in
162	  `references/theming.md`; the cross-cutting traps (partial brand overrides,
163	  a `ThemeProvider` that themes the whole page, controls on a brand background) live in
164	  `rules/hallucination-traps.md`.
165	- **Required setup is package-specific** (style imports, `ThemeProvider`,
166	  peer-deps). It lives in each package's root README under "Required setup" —
167	  read it once per package, do not rely on memory.
168	
169	## What NOT to do
170	
171	These are the five most common ways agents break Gravity UI code. They are
172	already implied by the rules above; this section exists as an explicit
173	stop-sign. If you are about to do any of these, stop and re-ground.
174	
175	- **Do not substitute non-Gravity libraries.** No MUI, Ant Design, plain
176	  `<input>`/`<button>`, or look-alike component libs. Use the `@gravity-ui/*`
177	  package the task needs.
178	- **Do not invent component APIs or props.** If a prop is not in the docs you
179	  read in Step 1, it does not exist — do not write `variant=`, `color=`,
180	  `name=` (on `Icon`), or a `header-3` variant. Use the documented prop or
181	  ask the user. See `rules/hallucination-traps.md`.
182	- **Do not use the `/llms/<pkg>/llms.txt` "latest" alias as a fallback.** It
183	  serves the newest major, which may differ from the installed one and have a
184	  different API. The versioned online fallback is the major-line URL
185	  (`/llms/<pkg>/<major>/llms.txt`); below that, go LOCAL.
186	- **Do not partial-brand.** Setting only `--g-color-base-brand` leaves
187	  selection, focus, links and contrast on the default accent — a mismatched
188	  UI. Override the full brand token set, on each theme you support.
189	- **Do not override internal markup with `[class*='…']` / ID selectors.**
190	  That's written against one DOM structure and breaks silently when the
191	  component changes. Climb the customization ladder
192	  (global token → component CSS API → narrow flagged hack) before ever
193	  touching structure.
194	
195	## Deeper material — read on demand
196	
197	These files live alongside this SKILL.md and load only when relevant:
198	
199	- `references/package-routing.md` — offline snapshot of the ecosystem catalog
200	  (`gravity-ui.com/llms.txt`), refreshed each skill release. Used as the
201	  offline fallback in Step 0.
202	- `references/theming.md` — verbatim copy of uikit's `docs/theming.md`:
203	  `--g-*` token layers, `ThemeProvider`, branding, custom themes, scoped
204	  themes, `uikit-themer`. The bundled copy may lag — read
205	  `node_modules/@gravity-ui/uikit/build/docs/guides/theming.md` for the
206	  version-matched file.
207	- `references/layout.md` — verbatim copy of uikit's `docs/layout.md`:
208	  spacing scale (`--g-spacing-*`), `Flex`/`Box`, `Row`/`Col`/`Container`
209	  grid, breakpoints, `useLayoutContext`.
210	- `references/icons.md` — finding an icon by image
211	  (`scripts/icon-image-search.sh`) or on gravity-ui.com/icons; the
212	  object-vs-string rendering rule.
213	- `rules/hallucination-traps.md` — Incorrect/Correct pairs for the most
214	  commonly invented APIs: typography variants (`header-3..6` don't exist, no
215	  `Heading`), the flex contract (`min-width:0`, who shrinks), theming traps
216	  (partial brand overrides, a `ThemeProvider` that themes the whole page, customization
217	  ladder), `Button view` not `variant`, `Icon data` not `name`. Per-component
218	  traps live in each package's `dist/docs`, not here.

176	  `<input>`/`<button>`, or look-alike component libs. Use the `@gravity-ui/*`
177	  package the task needs.

1	# Package routing — offline snapshot
2	
3	This is an offline snapshot of **https://gravity-ui.com/llms.txt**, the Gravity UI
4	ecosystem catalog. It exists so Step 0 of the skill works when the online catalog
5	is unreachable (air-gapped, corporate proxy, timeout).
6	
7	**Online is primary.** This snapshot may lag the site by one release — if you can
8	fetch `https://gravity-ui.com/llms.txt`, prefer it. Refresh this file at each
9	skill release by re-copying the catalog verbatim (generator = fetch the URL →

11	catalog body below the line; edit the source `llms.txt` instead. The decision
12	table above the line is hand-maintained and survives the sync.
13	
14	## Decision table — read this before the catalog
15	
16	Settle the common tasks here; the catalog below is the reference for everything else (and it is long:
17	its decisive entries sit near the end, so do not skim its top and default to `uikit`).
18	
19	| The task is… | Use | Not |
20	|---|---|---|
21	| A marketing / landing / promo page assembled from blocks (hero, features, CTA) | `@gravity-ui/page-constructor` (`PageConstructor` + `PageConstructorProvider`, block config) | hand-written sections from uikit primitives |
22	| A dashboard of freely arrangeable widgets | `@gravity-ui/dashkit` | a hand-rolled CSS grid, `react-grid-layout` |
23	| A table with sorting, checkbox selection, pagination | uikit `Table` + `withTableSorting` / `withTableSelection` + `Pagination` | `@gravity-ui/table` |
24	| A data grid that needs virtualization, column resizing / reordering, grouping, tree rows | `@gravity-ui/table` (TanStack-based) | uikit `Table` |
25	| A calendar, date / time / range picker | `@gravity-ui/date-components` (peer: `date-utils`) | a `Calendar` from uikit (does not exist), `react-datepicker` |
26	| Charts and data visualization | `@gravity-ui/charts` (`<Chart>`); `@gravity-ui/yagr` only for dense realtime series | `chartkit` (legacy wrapper), `recharts`, raw canvas |
27	| A Markdown / WYSIWYG editor | `@gravity-ui/markdown-editor` | `<textarea>` + custom preview |
28	| The app shell: aside navigation, header, footer | `@gravity-ui/navigation` (`AsideHeader`) | a hand-rolled `<aside>` |
29	| Interface language switching | uikit `configure({lang})` + `@gravity-ui/i18n` for app strings | `i18next`, `react-intl` |
30	
31	Everything not listed — buttons, forms, dialogs, toasts, menus, tabs, theming — is `@gravity-ui/uikit`.
32	If the package from the table is not installed yet, **install it** with the project's package manager (and
33	its documented peer deps) — a project that only has `uikit` is not a reason to build the thing by hand.
34	
35	---
36	
37	# Gravity UI
38	
39	Gravity UI is a open-source design system and ecosystem of React libraries for building web applications. This file is a compact catalog: pick a package, then fetch its per-package llms.txt for the full agent-facing docs. Read the user's `package.json` first and match the installed `@gravity-ui/*` versions — peer-version mismatches across the ecosystem are the most common failure.
40	
41	> **`@gravity-ui/uikit` MUST be installed in every Gravity UI project.** It is the base component and design-token library that every other `@gravity-ui/*` package builds on — without it, components render unstyled. Check the user's `package.json` first.
42	>
43	> **If it is not installed, stop and have the user install and configure it before doing anything else.** Setup and theming instructions: https://gravity-ui.com/llms/uikit/llms.txt
44	
45	> **Per-package docs are versioned.** Each package lives at `/llms/<package>/<version>/llms.txt` (exact version), `/llms/<package>/<major>/llms.txt` (latest of a major line), and `/llms/<package>/llms.txt` (latest). The links below point at `latest` — read the user's `package.json` and switch the URL to the installed version (or major) when it differs.
46	
47	> **Agent skill recommended.** A `gravity-ui` skill is available that helps route to the correct package and avoid common API mistakes. Consider installing it when working with Gravity UI:
48	>
49	> ```bash
50	npx skills add gravity-ui/skills
51	> ```
52	>
53	> It can help with tasks involving `@gravity-ui/*` imports, `ThemeProvider`, or `--g-` CSS tokens. Details: https://github.com/gravity-ui/skills
54	
55	## UIKit (primary) — `@gravity-ui/uikit`
56	
57	> If you need this library, read more at package [llms.txt](https://gravity-ui.com/llms/uikit/llms.txt)
58	> GitHub: [gravity-ui/uikit](https://github.com/gravity-ui/uikit)
59	
60	The base React component and design-token library for Gravity UI apps — controls, inputs, overlays, layout, and theming that every other @gravity-ui package builds on.
61	
62	#### When to use
63	
64	- Standard application UI: buttons, form controls, modals and popups, menus, tabs, labels, typography, and layout primitives.
65	- Selectable, navigable lists (`List`) and select controls (`Select`).
66	- The theming foundation of a Gravity UI app: `Provider`, design tokens, and CSS variables the rest of the `@gravity-ui/*` ecosystem expects to be present.
67	
68	#### When not to use
69	
70	- Tables and data grids (selection, sorting, virtualization, column resizing, grouping, reordering) — use [`@gravity-ui/table`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/table), a separate headless package. The `Table` component of uikit lives in `@gravity-ui/uikit/legacy` since v8 and is kept only for existing code.
71	- Charts and data visualization — use [`@gravity-ui/charts`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/charts) (`@gravity-ui/chartkit` is the legacy wrapper).
72	- Application navigation shells (aside header, footer, logo) — use [`@gravity-ui/navigation`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/navigation).
73	- Date pickers, calendars, and range controls — use [`@gravity-ui/date-components`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/date-components).
74	- The SVG icon set itself — use [`@gravity-ui/icons`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/icons); uikit only ships the `Icon` renderer.
75	
76	## AIKit — `@gravity-ui/aikit`
77	
78	> If you need this library, read more at package [llms.txt](https://gravity-ui.com/llms/aikit/llms.txt)
79	> GitHub: [gravity-ui/aikit](https://github.com/gravity-ui/aikit)
80	
81	A React component library for building AI chat interfaces, organized by Atomic Design (atoms → molecules → organisms → templates → pages) and SDK-agnostic — reach for it to assemble a chat UI (message lists, prompt input, tool calls, attachments) instead of composing those primitives out of `@gravity-ui/uikit` by hand.
82	
83	#### When to use
84	
85	- Building an AI/LLM chat UI (assistant/user/tool messages, prompt input with suggestions, attachment uploads, thinking states).
86	- Wanting ready-made chat layouts (`ChatContainer`, `MessageList`, `PromptInput`) plus hooks to customize behavior.
87	- Embedding into the Gravity UI ecosystem with shared theming via CSS variables.
88	
89	#### When not to use
90	
91	- For general-purpose UI primitives (buttons, inputs, modals), use [`@gravity-ui/uikit`](https://gravity-ui.com/uikit) directly — AIKit builds on top of it for chat-specific needs.
92	- To render rich markdown in messages, AIKit's `MarkdownRenderer` wraps [`@gravity-ui/markdown-editor`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/markdown-editor); for standalone markdown rendering use that package directly.
93	- For a single chat bubble without chat orchestration, a uikit `MarkdownRenderer`/text block is lighter than the full AIKit message pipeline.
94	
95	## App Layout — `@gravity-ui/app-layout`
96	
97	> If you need this library, read more at package [llms.txt](https://gravity-ui.com/llms/app-layout/llms.txt)
98	> GitHub: [gravity-ui/app-layout](https://github.com/gravity-ui/app-layout)
99	
100	HTML layout generator used in our SPA applications.
101	
102	## Axios wrapper — `@gravity-ui/axios-wrapper`
103	
104	> If you need this library, read more at package [llms.txt](https://gravity-ui.com/llms/axios-wrapper/llms.txt)
105	> GitHub: [gravity-ui/axios-wrapper](https://github.com/gravity-ui/axios-wrapper)
106	
107	Axios wrapper that provides automatic cancelling of concurrent requests.
108	
109	## Babel Preset — `@gravity-ui/babel-preset`
110	
111	> If you need this library, read more at package [llms.txt](https://gravity-ui.com/llms/babel-preset/llms.txt)
112	> GitHub: [gravity-ui/babel-preset](https://github.com/gravity-ui/babel-preset)
113	
114	Babel configuration preset for Gravity UI projects.
115	
116	## Blog Constructor — `@gravity-ui/blog-constructor`
117	
118	> If you need this library, read more at package [llms.txt](https://gravity-ui.com/llms/blog-constructor/llms.txt)
119	> GitHub: [gravity-ui/blog-constructor](https://github.com/gravity-ui/blog-constructor)
120	
121	A library based on the Page constructor library for creating blog-like services.
122	
123	## Browserslist Config — `@gravity-ui/browserslist-config`
124	
125	> If you need this library, read more at package [llms.txt](https://gravity-ui.com/llms/browserslist-config/llms.txt)
126	> GitHub: [gravity-ui/browserslist-config](https://github.com/gravity-ui/browserslist-config)
127	
128	Browserslist configuration preset used in our services.
129	
130	## ChartKit — `@gravity-ui/chartkit`
131	
132	> If you need this library, read more at package [llms.txt](https://gravity-ui.com/llms/chartkit/llms.txt)
133	> GitHub: [gravity-ui/chartkit](https://github.com/gravity-ui/chartkit)
134	
135	A plugin-dispatching React component that renders charts from multiple Gravity UI charting libraries through one `<ChartKit type="..." data={...} />` API — reach for it when you need a single lazy-loading entry point for mixed chart types, instead of importing each chart library directly.
136	
137	#### When to use
138	
139	- Rendering more than one charting engine (e.g. `gravity-charts` + `yagr`) behind one consistent component.
140	- Lazy-loading chart bundles — each plugin's renderer is `React.lazy`, so a library's code is only fetched when its chart type is actually shown.
141	- Bundling charts into a Gravity UI app that wants mobile-friendly tooltips and unified theming out of the box.
142	
143	#### When not to use
144	
145	- For a single chart type only, import [`@gravity-ui/charts`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/charts) (general) or [`@gravity-ui/yagr`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/yagr) (high-performance time-series) directly — the plugin registry is overhead for one engine.
146	- To compose a dashboard grid of widgets, use [`@gravity-ui/dashkit`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/dashkit) — ChartKit renders a chart; DashKit arranges many widgets.
147	
148	## Charts — `@gravity-ui/charts`
149	
150	> If you need this library, read more at package [llms.txt](https://gravity-ui.com/llms/charts/llms.txt)
151	> GitHub: [gravity-ui/charts](https://github.com/gravity-ui/charts)
152	
153	A declarative React charting library for Gravity UI apps — render line, area, bar, pie, scatter, treemap, and other charts from a single `data` config, themed to match the rest of the app.
154	
155	#### When to use
156	
157	- Standard business charts: `line`, `area`, `bar-x`/`bar-y`, `pie`, `scatter`, `treemap`, `waterfall`, `sankey`, `radar`, `heatmap`, `funnel`, `x-range`.
158	- Visualizations that must follow Gravity UI theming (light/dark) and share tokens with a `@gravity-ui/uikit` app.
159	- Rendering a chart from declarative data rather than drawing imperatively.
160	
161	#### When not to use
162	
163	- Projects still on `@gravity-ui/chartkit` — that is the older adapter-based wrapper (YAGR/Highcharts/D3); this package is the modern standalone renderer and is not a drop-in replacement.
164	- Plain tabular data — use [`@gravity-ui/table`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/table).
165	- Non-React or server-only rendering — `Chart` renders React SVG and needs the DOM.
166	
167	## Components — `@gravity-ui/components`
168	
169	> If you need this library, read more at package [llms.txt](https://gravity-ui.com/llms/components/llms.txt)
170	> GitHub: [gravity-ui/components](https://github.com/gravity-ui/components)
171	
172	The composite-component layer of Gravity UI — ready-made form rows, confirmation dialogs, notifications, stories, galleries and similar product-level widgets assembled from `@gravity-ui/uikit` primitives, so you do not rebuild them by hand.
173	
174	#### When to use
175	
176	- Form layout: `FormRow` (label + field + description) instead of a hand-made label/input wrapper.
177	- Confirmation flows: `ConfirmDialog` instead of composing `Dialog` with two buttons yourself.
178	- Product widgets: `Notifications`, `Stories` / `StoriesGroup`, `ChangelogDialog`, `OnboardingMenu`, `PromoSheet`, `CookieConsent`, `Reactions`, `SharePopover`, `StoreBadge`.
179	- Data helpers: `InfiniteScroll`, `ItemSelector`, `DelayedTextInput`, `TokenizedInput`, `Gallery`.
180	
181	#### When not to use
182	
183	- Basic controls, overlays, layout and theming — use [`@gravity-ui/uikit`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/uikit) directly; this package only adds composites on top of it.
184	- Data grids — use [`@gravity-ui/table`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/table); there is no table here.
185	- Date pickers and calendars — use [`@gravity-ui/date-components`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/date-components).
186	- Application navigation shells (aside header, footer) — use [`@gravity-ui/navigation`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/navigation).
187	- Schema-driven forms — use [`@gravity-ui/dynamic-forms`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/dynamic-forms); `FormRow` is only a layout row.
188	
189	## DashKit — `@gravity-ui/dashkit`
190	
191	> If you need this library, read more at package [llms.txt](https://gravity-ui.com/llms/dashkit/llms.txt)
192	> GitHub: [gravity-ui/dashkit](https://github.com/gravity-ui/dashkit)
193	
194	A dashboard grid composer that arranges resizable, draggable widgets in a responsive grid via a plugin system — reach for it when you build a user-editable dashboard (add/move/resize/delete widgets) instead of placing individual charts or panels by hand.
195	
196	#### When to use
197	
198	- Rendering a configurable dashboard where widgets are positioned, resized, and rearranged on a grid (built on `react-grid-layout`).
199	- User-editable layouts: adding/removing widgets from an action panel, drag-and-drop, edit mode with overlay controls.
200	- Plugin-based widgets where each widget type (title, text, chart, custom) is registered once and driven by a `config`.
201	
202	#### When not to use
203	
204	- For a single, fixed chart or panel, use [`@gravity-ui/charts`](https://gravity-ui.com/charts) or [`@gravity-ui/chartkit`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/chartkit) directly — the grid/plugin machinery is overhead for one widget.
205	- For a general-purpose responsive grid that is not a widget dashboard, use `react-grid-layout` directly.
206	- For embedding ChartKit-backed chart widgets inside a DashKit dashboard, DashKit is the shell; it still relies on [`@gravity-ui/chartkit`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/chartkit) to render the actual charts.
207	
208	## Data Source — `@gravity-ui/data-source`
209	
210	> If you need this library, read more at package [llms.txt](https://gravity-ui.com/llms/data-source/llms.txt)
211	> GitHub: [gravity-ui/data-source](https://github.com/gravity-ui/data-source)
212	
213	A wrapper around data fetching.
214	
215	## Date Components — `@gravity-ui/date-components`
216	
217	> If you need this library, read more at package [llms.txt](https://gravity-ui.com/llms/date-components/llms.txt)
218	> GitHub: [gravity-ui/date-components](https://github.com/gravity-ui/date-components)
219	
220	React date and time controls for Gravity UI apps — date/time pickers, calendars, and absolute/relative range selectors built on `@gravity-ui/date-utils`.
221	
222	#### When to use
223	
224	- A single date or date-time input: `DatePicker`, `DateField`.
225	- Calendars for month/day selection: `Calendar`, `CalendarView`.
226	- Date ranges: `RangeDatePicker`, `RangeCalendar`, `RangeDateField`.
227	- Relative and mixed absolute/relative ranges (e.g. "last 7 days"): `RelativeDatePicker`, `RelativeRangeDatePicker`, `RelativeDateField`.
228	
229	#### When not to use
230	
231	- Plain text or number inputs, buttons, or other generic controls — use [`@gravity-ui/uikit`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/uikit).
232	- Low-level date math, parsing, formatting, or timezone handling without UI — use [`@gravity-ui/date-utils`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/date-utils) directly.
233	
234	## Date Utils — `@gravity-ui/date-utils`
235	
236	> If you need this library, read more at package [llms.txt](https://gravity-ui.com/llms/date-utils/llms.txt)
237	> GitHub: [gravity-ui/date-utils](https://github.com/gravity-ui/date-utils)
238	
239	Timezone-aware date/time helpers — parsing (including relative expressions like `now-1d/d`), formatting, and locale management — without any UI, reach for it when you need to compute and format dates reliably across time zones instead of pulling in a full UI calendar.
240	
241	#### When to use
242	
243	- Parsing absolute or relative date expressions (`'now-1d'`, `'now/d'`) into a timezone-aware `dateTime` object.
244	- Formatting dates for display in the user's timezone with locale support.
245	- Sharing date logic between server (Node) and client (React) code — the package has no React dependency.
246

37	# Gravity UI
38	
39	Gravity UI is a open-source design system and ecosystem of React libraries for building web applications. This file is a compact catalog: pick a package, then fetch its per-package llms.txt for the full agent-facing docs. Read the user's `package.json` first and match the installed `@gravity-ui/*` versions — peer-version mismatches across the ecosystem are the most common failure.
40	
41	> **`@gravity-ui/uikit` MUST be installed in every Gravity UI project.** It is the base component and design-token library that every other `@gravity-ui/*` package builds on — without it, components render unstyled. Check the user's `package.json` first.
42	>
43	> **If it is not installed, stop and have the user install and configure it before doing anything else.** Setup and theming instructions: https://gravity-ui.com/llms/uikit/llms.txt
44	
45	> **Per-package docs are versioned.** Each package lives at `/llms/<package>/<version>/llms.txt` (exact version), `/llms/<package>/<major>/llms.txt` (latest of a major line), and `/llms/<package>/llms.txt` (latest). The links below point at `latest` — read the user's `package.json` and switch the URL to the installed version (or major) when it differs.
46	
47	> **Agent skill recommended.** A `gravity-ui` skill is available that helps route to the correct package and avoid common API mistakes. Consider installing it when working with Gravity UI:

55	## UIKit (primary) — `@gravity-ui/uikit`
56	
57	> If you need this library, read more at package [llms.txt](https://gravity-ui.com/llms/uikit/llms.txt)
58	> GitHub: [gravity-ui/uikit](https://github.com/gravity-ui/uikit)

60	The base React component and design-token library for Gravity UI apps — controls, inputs, overlays, layout, and theming that every other @gravity-ui package builds on.
61	
62	#### When to use
63	
64	- Standard application UI: buttons, form controls, modals and popups, menus, tabs, labels, typography, and layout primitives.
65	- Selectable, navigable lists (`List`) and select controls (`Select`).
66	- The theming foundation of a Gravity UI app: `Provider`, design tokens, and CSS variables the rest of the `@gravity-ui/*` ecosystem expects to be present.

The `Table` component of uikit lives in `@gravity-ui/uikit/legacy` since v8 and is kept only for existing code.
71	- Charts and data visualization — use [`@gravity-ui/charts`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/charts) (`@gravity-ui/chartkit` is the legacy wrapper).

1	# @gravity-ui/navigation documentation
2	
3	Documentation for the **installed** version of `@gravity-ui/navigation`.
4	Your training data may be outdated — these files are the source of truth.
5	
6	Paths are relative to this file (`node_modules/@gravity-ui/navigation/build/docs/`).
7	
8	## For AI agents
9	
10	Application-shell navigation components for Gravity UI apps — the collapsible `AsideHeader` sidebar plus footers, drawers, logo, hotkeys and settings panels that frame a whole page.
11	
12	### When to use
13	
14	- The app's primary navigation frame: `AsideHeader` (collapsible side navigation) with `menuItems`, subheader, and footer sections.
15	- Supporting shell UI: `Drawer`/`DrawerItem`, `Footer`/`MobileFooter`, `MobileHeader`, `HotkeysPanel`, `Settings`, `ActionBar`, `Logo`.
16	- Laying out page content inside the navigation frame via `renderContent` / `PageLayout`.
17	
18	### When not to use
19	
20	- Generic in-page controls (buttons, tabs, menus, breadcrumbs) — use [`@gravity-ui/uikit`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/uikit); this package is the outer app chrome, not general components.
21	- Rendering the page body itself from config — use [`@gravity-ui/page-constructor`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/page-constructor).
22	- Client-side routing — this provides the navigation UI only; wire clicks to your own router.
23	
24	### Common pitfalls
25	
26	- **`AsideHeader` is controlled.** You must own the collapsed state with `compact` and update it in `onChangeCompact`; passing `compact` without the handler freezes the sidebar.
27	- **Menu items are `menuItems`, keyed by `id`.** Each item is `{id, title, icon, current, onItemClick}`; `icon` takes an icon component (e.g. from `@gravity-ui/icons`), not a string name.
28	- **Peer dependencies are required.** `@gravity-ui/uikit`, `@gravity-ui/icons`, and `@bem-react/classname` must be installed alongside `react`/`react-dom`.
29	- **Needs uikit setup.** Render inside `ThemeProvider` and import `@gravity-ui/uikit/styles/styles.css`, or the shell renders unstyled.
30	- **Page content goes through `renderContent`.** Render your routed content via the `renderContent` prop / `PageLayout`, not as `children`.
31	
32	## Install
33	
34	```bash
35	npm install @gravity-ui/navigation
36	```
37	
38	Ensure that peer dependencies are installed in your project
39	
40	```bash
41	npm install --dev @gravity-ui/uikit@^7.2.0 @gravity-ui/icons@^2.2.0 @bem-react/classname@^1.6.0 react@^19.0.0 react-dom@^19.0.0
42	```
43	
44	## Usage
45	
46	Render `AsideHeader` as the app shell. It is a controlled component — you own the collapsed state via `compact`/`onChangeCompact` — and your page content goes through `renderContent`. Set up `@gravity-ui/uikit` styles and `ThemeProvider` first (see the [uikit styles guide](https://github.com/gravity-ui/uikit?tab=readme-ov-file#styles)).
47	
48	```tsx
49	import React from 'react';
50	import {AsideHeader} from '@gravity-ui/navigation';
51	import {Gear, House} from '@gravity-ui/icons';
52	import {ThemeProvider} from '@gravity-ui/uikit';
53	
54	import '@gravity-ui/uikit/styles/styles.css';
55	
56	export function App() {
57	  const [compact, setCompact] = React.useState(false);
58	
59	  return (
60	    <ThemeProvider theme="light">
61	      <AsideHeader
62	        logo={{text: 'My App', href: '/'}}
63	        compact={compact}
64	        onChangeCompact={setCompact}
65	        menuItems={[
66	          {id: 'home', title: 'Home', icon: House, current: true},
67	          {id: 'settings', title: 'Settings', icon: Gear},
68	        ]}
69	        renderContent={() => <main>Page content</main>}
70	      />
71	    </ThemeProvider>
72	  );
73	}
74	```
75	
76	## Components
77	
78	- [ActionBar](./components/ActionBar.md) — The component is a flexible horizontal bar that provides a standardized layout for arranging navigation elements, actions, and informational content within an application. It serves as a container for organizing UI elements like breadcrumbs, buttons, and dropdown menus into defined sections and groups.
79	- [AsideHeader](./components/AsideHeader.md) — AsideHeader is provided a flexible and customizable navigation experience within your application. Users can easily customize the appearance of the sidebar to match their branding colors also to add personalized links, icons that cater specifically to their application's functionality.
80	- [AsideHeader/components/AllPagesPanel](./components/AsideHeader/components/AllPagesPanel.md) — A navigation panel for managing and organizing application pages in the middle (menuItems) section of AsideHeader component. Panel provides drag-and-drop reordering, visibility toggles, pin/unpin and category grouping of menu items.
81	- [Footer](./components/Footer.md) — The page footer components. Use Footer for the desktop version and MobileFooter for the mobile version. Both components have the same properties.
82	- [HotkeysPanel](./components/HotkeysPanel.md) — A navigation panel for hotkeys documentation. The panel displays a set of hotkeys for your application with a description of their purpose.
83	- [Logo](./components/Logo.md) — Logo icon is wrapped in UIKit Button, text is wrapped in HTML tag a or div, when passing hasWrapper prop.
84	- [MobileHeader](./components/MobileHeader.md) — Header for Mobile navigation. MobileHeader provides maintaining Panels except for Modals.
85	- [Settings](./components/Settings.md) — The Settings component provides the layout for a settings panel with the following features.
86	
87	## Hooks
88	
89	- [useOverflowingHorizontalListItems](./hooks/useOverflowingHorizontalListItems.md) — A hook for determining which horizontal list items stay visible and which collapse into an overflow "more" dropdown.

82	- [HotkeysPanel](./components/HotkeysPanel.md) — A navigation panel for hotkeys documentation. The panel displays a set of hotkeys for your application with a description of their purpose.
83	- [Logo](./components/Logo.md) — Logo icon is wrapped in UIKit Button, text is wrapped in HTML tag a or div, when passing hasWrapper prop.
84	- [MobileHeader](./components/MobileHeader.md) — Header for Mobile navigation. MobileHeader provides maintaining Panels except for Modals.
85	- [Settings](./components/Settings.md) — The Settings component provides the layout for a settings panel with the following features.
86	
87	## Hooks

89	- [useOverflowingHorizontalListItems](./hooks/useOverflowingHorizontalListItems.md) — A hook for determining which horizontal list items stay visible and which collapse into an overflow "more" dropdown.

1	# @gravity-ui/table documentation
2	
3	Documentation for the **installed** version of `@gravity-ui/table`.
4	Your training data may be outdated — these files are the source of truth.
5	
6	Paths are relative to this file (`node_modules/@gravity-ui/table/build/docs/`).
7	
8	## For AI agents
9	
10	A headless, TanStack-Table-powered data grid for Gravity UI apps — reach for it for sortable, selectable, groupable, reorderable, and virtualized tables instead of composing raw markup on top of uikit's basic `Table`.
11	
12	### When to use
13	
14	- Large datasets that need row or window virtualization (`useRowVirtualizer`, `useWindowRowVirtualizer`).
15	- Column sorting, resizing, reordering (`ColumnReorderingProvider`), pinning, and per-user column settings (`TableSettings`).
16	- Row selection (single/multi, ranged) and tree/grouped rows with expandable cells.
17	
18	### When not to use
19	
20	- A simple, static table with a handful of rows and no advanced features — uikit's built-in `Table` from [`@gravity-ui/uikit`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/uikit) is lighter.
21	- A non-tabular list — use `List` from [`@gravity-ui/uikit`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/uikit).
22	- Spreadsheet-style inline cell editing — this grid is read/display-focused, not an editable spreadsheet.
23	
24	### Common pitfalls
25	
26	- **You build the table with `useTable`, then render `<Table table={table} />`.** The main prop is `table` (the instance), not `data`/`columns` directly on `<Table>`; pass `data` and `columns` to `useTable`.
27	- **Types come from the `@gravity-ui/table/tanstack` subpath.** Import `ColumnDef`, `RowSelectionState`, `SortingState`, etc. from `@gravity-ui/table/tanstack`, not from the package root.
28	- **Sorting needs an accessor.** A column must have `accessorKey`/`accessorFn` for sorting to work; set `enableSorting` and provide `getRowId`.
29	- **React 19 + React Compiler can skip re-renders.** This is an upstream TanStack Table issue — add the `'use no memo'` directive to the component or memoize `data`.
30	- **Range selection breaks with nested rows.** Ranged selection is undefined behavior when the table has grouped/nested rows; use `useRowSelectionFixedHandler` for correct parent-checkbox state with grouping.
31	
32	## Install
33	
34	```shell
35	npm install --save @gravity-ui/table
36	```
37	
38	## Usage
39	
40	```tsx
41	import React from 'react';
42	import {Table, useTable} from '@gravity-ui/table';
43	import type {ColumnDef} from '@gravity-ui/table/tanstack';
44	
45	interface Person {
46	  id: string;
47	  name: string;
48	  age: number;
49	}
50	
51	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
52	  {accessorKey: 'name', header: 'Name', size: 100},
53	  {accessorKey: 'age', header: 'Age', size: 100},
54	];
55	
56	const data: Person[] = [
57	  {id: 'name', name: 'John', age: 23},
58	  {id: 'age', name: 'Michael', age: 27},
59	];
60	
61	const BasicExample = () => {
62	  const table = useTable({
63	    columns,
64	    data,
65	  });
66	
67	  return <Table table={table} />;
68	};
69	```
70	
71	### Components
72	
73	There are two Table components that you can use:
74	
75	- `BaseTable` - a component with basic styles only;
76	- `Table` - a component with Gravity UI based styles.
77	
78	#### Row selection
79	
80	```tsx
81	import {selectionColumn} from '@gravity-ui/table';
82	import type {RowSelectionState} from '@gravity-ui/table/tanstack';
83	
84	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
85	  selectionColumn as ColumnDef<Person>,
86	  // ...other columns
87	];
88	
89	const data: Person[] = [
90	  /* ... */
91	];
92	
93	const RowSelectionExample = () => {
94	  const [rowSelection, setRowSelection] = React.useState<RowSelectionState>({});
95	
96	  const table = useTable({
97	    columns,
98	    data,
99	    enableRowSelection: true,
100	    enableMultiRowSelection: true,
101	    onRowSelectionChange: setRowSelection,
102	    state: {
103	      rowSelection,
104	    },
105	  });
106	
107	  return <Table table={table} />;
108	};
109	```
110	
111	To use grouping with selection, use `useRowSelectionFixedHandler` hook. Without it parent row checkbox state will be wrong. https://github.com/TanStack/table/issues/4878
112	
113	#### Custom Ranged Selection Column
114	
115	The `useToggleRangeSelectionHandler` hook returns a change handler that listens for Shift+click events and performs ranged row selection. It needs to be passed a `CellContext` instance in order to have access to the table's and row's internal states.
116	
117	```tsx
118	import React, {type ChangeEvent, useCallback, useState} from 'react';
119	
120	import {Table, useToggleRangeSelectionHandler, useTable} from '@gravity-ui/table';
121	import type {CellContext, ColumnDef, RowSelectionState} from '@gravity-ui/table/tanstack';
122	import {Checkbox, type CheckboxProps} from '@gravity-ui/uikit';
123	
124	type CustomRangedSelectionCheckboxProps = Omit<CheckboxProps, 'onChange'> & {
125	  cellContext: CellContext<unknown, unknown>;
126	};
127	
128	const CustomRangedSelectionCheckbox = ({
129	  className,
130	  cellContext,
131	  ...restProps
132	}: CustomRangedSelectionCheckboxProps) => {
133	  const rowToggleRangedSelectionHandler = useToggleRangeSelectionHandler(cellContext);
134	
135	  const handleChange = useCallback(
136	    (event: ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>): void => {
137	      rowToggleRangedSelectionHandler(event);
138	    },
139	    [rowToggleRangedSelectionHandler],
140	  );
141	
142	  return <Checkbox {...restProps} onChange={handleChange} />;
143	};
144	
145	const customSelectionColumn: ColumnDef<unknown> = {
146	  id: '_select',
147	  header: ({table}) => (
148	    <Checkbox
149	      size="l"
150	      checked={table.getIsAllRowsSelected()}
151	      indeterminate={table.getIsSomeRowsSelected()}
152	      onChange={table.getToggleAllRowsSelectedHandler()}
153	    />
154	  ),
155	  cell: (cellContext) => (
156	    <CustomRangedSelectionCheckbox
157	      size="l"
158	      checked={cellContext.row.getIsSelected()}
159	      disabled={!cellContext.row.getCanSelect()}
160	      indeterminate={cellContext.row.getIsSomeSelected()}
161	      cellContext={cellContext}
162	    />
163	  ),
164	  size: 41,
165	  maxSize: 41,
166	  minSize: 41,
167	  enableResizing: false,
168	  enableSorting: false,
169	};
170	
171	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
172	  customSelectionColumn as ColumnDef<Person>,
173	  // ...other columns
174	];
175	
176	const data: Person[] = [
177	  /* ... */
178	];
179	
180	const RowRangedSelectionExample = () => {
181	  const [rowSelection, setRowSelection] = useState<RowSelectionState>({});
182	
183	  const table = useTable({
184	    columns,
185	    data,
186	    enableRowSelection: true,
187	    enableMultiRowSelection: true,
188	    onRowSelectionChange: setRowSelection,
189	    state: {
190	      rowSelection,
191	    },
192	  });
193	
194	  return <Table table={table} />;
195	};
196	```
197	
198	There is also a `RangedSelectionCheckbox` component, which internally uses the hook and accepts a `CellContext` instance as a prop. This component provides a shorthand for adding ranged selection functionality to custom selection columns.
199	
200	```tsx
201	import type {ColumnDef} from '@gravity-ui/table/tanstack';
202	import {RangedSelectionCheckbox, SelectionCheckbox} from '@gravity-ui/table';
203	
204	export const selectionColumn: ColumnDef<unknown> = {
205	  id: '_select',
206	  header: ({table}) => (
207	    <SelectionCheckbox
208	      checked={table.getIsAllRowsSelected()}
209	      disabled={!table.options.enableRowSelection}
210	      indeterminate={table.getIsSomeRowsSelected()}
211	      onChange={table.getToggleAllRowsSelectedHandler()}
212	    />
213	  ),
214	  cell: (cellContext) => (
215	    <RangedSelectionCheckbox
216	      checked={cellContext.row.getIsSelected()}
217	      disabled={!cellContext.row.getCanSelect()}
218	      indeterminate={cellContext.row.getIsSomeSelected()}
219	      cellContext={cellContext}
220	    />
221	  ),
222	  meta: {
223	    hideInSettings: true,
224	  },
225	  size: 32,
226	  minSize: 32,
227	};
228	```
229	
230	By default, the selection column generated with `selectionColumn` includes ranged selection functionality.
231	
232	```tsx
233	import {selectionColumn} from '@gravity-ui/table';
234	import type {ColumnDef} from '@gravity-ui/table/tanstack';
235	
236	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
237	  selectionColumn as ColumnDef<Person>,
238	  // ...other columns
239	];
240	```
241	
242	**Note**: If the table contains nested rows, range selection will not work. At the moment, this is considered undefined behavior.
243	
244	#### Sorting
245	
246	Learn about the column properties in the react-table [docs](https://tanstack.com/table/v8/docs/guide/sorting)
247	
248	```tsx
249	import type {SortingState} from '@gravity-ui/table/tanstack';
250	
251	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
252	  /* ... */
253	];
254	
255	const data: Person[] = [
256	  /* ... */
257	];
258	
259	const SortingExample = () => {
260	  const [sorting, setSorting] = React.useState<SortingState>([]);
261	
262	  // Your column MUST have accessorFn for sorting to be enabled
263	
264	  const table = useTable({
265	    columns,
266	    data,
267	    enableSorting: true,
268	    getRowId: (item) => item.id,
269	    onSortingChange: setSorting,
270	    state: {
271	      sorting,
272	    },
273	  });
274	
275	  return <Table table={table} />;
276	};
277	```
278	
279	If you want to sort the elements manually pass `manualSorting` property:
280	
281	```tsx
282	const table = useTable({
283	  // ...
284	  manualSorting: true,
285	});
286	```
287	
288	#### Grouping
289	
290	```tsx
291	import type {ExpandedState, Row} from '@gravity-ui/table/tanstack';
292	
293	interface Person {
294	  id: string;
295	  name: string;
296	  age: number;
297	}
298	
299	interface PersonGroup {
300	  id: string;
301	  name: string;
302	  items: Person[];
303	}
304	
305	type Item = PersonGroup | Person;
306	
307	const columns: ColumnDef<Item>[] = [
308	  {accessorKey: 'name', header: 'Name', size: 200},
309	  {accessorKey: 'age', header: 'Age', size: 100},
310	];
311	
312	const data: Item[] = [
313	  {
314	    id: 'friends',
315	    name: 'Friends',
316	    items: [
317	      {id: 'nick', name: 'Nick', age: 25},
318	      {id: 'tom', name: 'Tom', age: 21},
319	    ],
320	  },
321	  {
322	    id: 'relatives',
323	    name: 'Relatives',
324	    items: [
325	      {id: 'john', name: 'John', age: 23},
326	      {id: 'michael', name: 'Michael', age: 27},
327	    ],
328	  },
329	];
330	
331	const getGroupTitle = (row: Row<Item>) => row.getValue<string>('name');
332	
333	const GroupingExample = () => {
334	  const [expanded, setExpanded] = React.useState<ExpandedState>({});
335	
336	  const table = useTable({
337	    columns,
338	    data,
339	    enableExpanding: true,
340	    getSubRows: (item) => ('items' in item ? item.items : undefined),
341	    onExpandedChange: setExpanded,
342	    state: {
343	      expanded,
344	    },
345	  });
346	
347	  return <Table table={table} getGroupTitle={getGroupTitle} />;
348	};
349	```
350	
351	To use grouping with selection, use `useRowSelectionFixedHandler` hook. Without it parent row checkbox state will be wrong. https://github.com/TanStack/table/issues/4878
352	
353	To enable nesting styles, pass `withNestingStyles = true` in the column configuration.
354	
355	Nesting indicators can be disabled by passing `showTreeDepthIndicators = false`.
356	
357	To add a control for expanding/collapsing rows, wrap the cell content with the `TreeExpandableCell` component or with your similar custom component:
358	
359	```tsx
360	import {TreeExpandableCell} from '@gravity-ui/table';
361	
362	const columns: ColumnDef<Item>[] = [
363	  {
364	    accessorKey: 'name',
365	    header: 'Name',
366	    size: 200,
367	    showTreeDepthIndicators: false,
368	    withNestingStyles: true,
369	    cell: ({row, info}) => (
370	      <TreeExpandableCell row={row}>{info.getValue<string>()}</TreeExpandableCell>
371	    ),
372	  },
373	  // ...other columns
374	];
375	```
376	
377	#### Reordering
378	
379	```tsx
380	import type {ReorderingProviderProps} from '@gravity-ui/table';
381	import {dragHandleColumn, ReorderingProvider} from '@gravity-ui/table';
382	
383	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
384	  dragHandleColumn,
385	  // ...other columns
386	];
387	
388	const data: Person[] = [
389	  /* ... */
390	];
391	
392	const ReorderingExample = () => {
393	  const table = useTable({
394	    columns,
395	    data,
396	    getRowId: (item) => item.id,
397	  });
398	
399	  const handleReorder = React.useCallback<
400	    NonNullable<ReorderingProviderProps<Person>['onReorder']>
401	  >(
402	    ({
403	      draggedItemKey,
404	      targetItemKey,
405	      baseItemKey,
406	      baseNextItemKey,
407	      enableNesting,
408	      nextChild,
409	      pullFromParent,
410	    }) => {
411	      // ...
412	    },
413	    [],
414	  );
415	
416	  return (
417	    <ReorderingProvider table={table} onReorder={handleReorder}>
418	      <Table table={table} />
419	    </ReorderingProvider>
420	  );
421	};
422	```
423	
424	#### Reordering without a drag handle
425	
426	Set `dragWithoutHandle` to use the whole row as the drag activator and omit
427	`dragHandleColumn` from the column definitions:
428	
429	```tsx
430	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
431	  {accessorKey: 'name', header: 'Name'},
432	  {accessorKey: 'age', header: 'Age'},
433	];
434	
435	return (
436	  <ReorderingProvider table={table} dragWithoutHandle onReorder={handleReorder}>
437	    <Table table={table} />
438	  </ReorderingProvider>
439	);
440	```
441	
442	The pointer must move by 8 pixels before dragging starts, so regular row and control clicks keep
443	working. To exclude a custom part of a row from starting a drag, call `preventDefault()` in its
444	`onPointerDown` handler.
445	
446	`ReorderingProvider` enables dnd-kit's vertical auto-scroll by default. Pass `autoScroll={false}`
447	when the application supplies its own drag auto-scroll implementation; running both at once can
448	produce competing scroll writes.
449	
450	Custom drag handles should read `attributes`, `listeners`, and `setActivatorNodeRef` from
451	`DraggableRowContext` and attach them to the handle element. This reuses the row's DnD
452	registration. Do not call `useSortable` again with the same row id: a handle mounted later
453	by virtualization would replace the row's registered DOM node.
454	
455	#### Keyboard reordering and accessibility
456	
457	`ReorderingProvider` supports keyboard row dragging.
458	Focus a drag handle, press Space or Enter to pick up the row, use the arrow keys to move it, and press
459	Space or Enter to drop it. Escape cancels the move.
460	Keyboard dragging applies only to rows; keyboard interactions with column headers remain unchanged.
461	
462	Use `accessibility` to customize dnd-kit's screen reader instructions, announcements, announcement
463	container, and focus restoration for both keyboard and pointer dragging.
464	When row and column providers are nested, they share the same DnD context and accessibility settings;
465	provider order does not matter.
466	
467	```tsx
468	<ReorderingProvider
469	  table={table}
470	  onReorder={handleReorder}
471	  accessibility={{
472	    screenReaderInstructions: {
473	      draggable:
474	        'Press Space to pick up a row, arrow keys to move, Enter to drop, or Escape to cancel.',
475	    },
476	  }}
477	>
478	  <Table table={table} />
479	</ReorderingProvider>
480	```
481	
482	#### Column reordering
483	
484	Wrap the table with `ColumnReorderingProvider` to enable drag-and-drop reordering of columns by their headers.
485	
486	```tsx
487	import {ColumnReorderingProvider} from '@gravity-ui/table';
488	
489	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
490	  {accessorKey: 'name', header: 'Name', size: 100},
491	  {accessorKey: 'age', header: 'Age', size: 100},
492	];
493	
494	const ColumnReorderingExample = () => {
495	  const table = useTable({
496	    columns,
497	    data,
498	    getRowId: (item) => item.id,
499	  });
500	
501	  return (
502	    <ColumnReorderingProvider table={table}>
503	      <Table table={table} />
504	    </ColumnReorderingProvider>
505	  );
506	};
507	```
508	
509	### Row and column reordering together
510	
511	Nest `ColumnReorderingProvider` and `ReorderingProvider` to enable both drag axes at once. The order of providers does not matter — they share a single dnd-kit context internally.
512	
513	```tsx
514	import type {ColumnReorderingProviderProps, ReorderingProviderProps} from '@gravity-ui/table';
515	import {ColumnReorderingProvider, ReorderingProvider, dragHandleColumn} from '@gravity-ui/table';
516	
517	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
518	  dragHandleColumn,
519	  {accessorKey: 'name', header: 'Name'},
520	  {accessorKey: 'age', header: 'Age'},
521	];
522	
523	const CombinedReorderingExample = () => {
524	  const [data, setData] = React.useState(initialData);
525	  const [columnOrder, setColumnOrder] = React.useState<string[]>([]);
526	
527	  const table = useTable({
528	    columns,
529	    data,
530	    getRowId: (item) => item.id,
531	    state: {columnOrder},
532	    onColumnOrderChange: setColumnOrder,
533	  });
534	
535	  const handleRowReorder = React.useCallback<
536	    NonNullable<ReorderingProviderProps<Person>['onReorder']>
537	  >(({draggedItemKey, baseItemKey}) => {
538	    // update data array
539	  }, []);
540	
541	  const handleColumnReorder = React.useCallback<
542	    NonNullable<ColumnReorderingProviderProps<Person>['onReorder']>
543	  >(({columnOrder}) => {
544	    setColumnOrder(columnOrder);
545	  }, []);
546	
547	  return (
548	    <ColumnReorderingProvider table={table} onReorder={handleColumnReorder}>
549	      <ReorderingProvider table={table} onReorder={handleRowReorder}>
550	        <Table table={table} />
551	      </ReorderingProvider>
552	    </ColumnReorderingProvider>
553	  );
554	};
555	```
556	
557	If you control `columnOrder` yourself (e.g. to persist it), pass `onReorder` and apply the resulting order:
558	
559	```tsx
560	const [columnOrder, setColumnOrder] = React.useState<string[]>([]);
561	
562	const table = useTable({
563	  columns,
564	  data,
565	  state: {columnOrder},
566	  onColumnOrderChange: setColumnOrder,
567	});
568	
569	return (
570	  <ColumnReorderingProvider
571	    table={table}
572	    onReorder={({columnOrder}) => setColumnOrder(columnOrder)}
573	  >
574	    <Table table={table} />
575	  </ColumnReorderingProvider>
576	);
577	```
578	
579	CSS API:
580	
581	| CSS variable                                 | Default                       | Description                      |
582	| -------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
583	| `--gt-table-reordering-insertion-line-color` | `#4d8bff`                     | Color of the drop insertion line |
584	| `--gt-table-reordering-insertion-line-width` | `2px`                         | Width of the drop insertion line |
585	| `--gt-table-reordering-dragged-opacity`      | `0.4`                         | Opacity of the dragged column    |
586	| `--gt-table-drag-overlay-background`         | `#fff`                        | Drag preview background          |
587	| `--gt-table-drag-overlay-shadow`             | `0 3px 12px rgba(0,0,0,0.15)` | Drag preview box-shadow          |
588	| `--gt-table-drag-overlay-border-radius`      | `6px`                         | Drag preview border radius       |
589	
590	To forbid reordering a specific column, set `enableColumnReordering: false` in its column definition. Placeholder (grouped) columns are not draggable. Use `activationDistance` (default `8`) to tune how far the pointer must move before a drag starts, which keeps header clicks (like sorting) working.
591	
592	Pinned columns can be reordered too, but only among themselves: a column can be moved within the left-pinned group, the right-pinned group, or the center (non-pinned) group — it never crosses a pin boundary by dragging.
593	
594	```tsx
595	<ColumnReorderingProvider
596	  table={table}
597	  onReorder={({columnOrder, columnPinning, pinned}) => {
598	    if (pinned) {
599	      setColumnPinning(columnPinning);
600	    } else {
601	      setColumnOrder(columnOrder);
602	    }
603	  }}
604	>
605	  <Table table={table} />
606	</ColumnReorderingProvider>
607	```
608	
609	While dragging:
610	
611	- a floating preview of the column (its header plus the first rows) follows the pointer in a drag overlay;
612	- the dragged column becomes semi-transparent;
613	- a blue insertion line is drawn where the column will be dropped;
614	
615	```tsx
616	<ColumnReorderingProvider
617	  table={table}
618	  autoScroll
619	  dragOverlayRowCount={10}
620	  renderDragOverlay={({columnId}) => <CustomColumnPreview columnId={columnId} />}
621	>
622	  <Table table={table} />
623	</ColumnReorderingProvider>
624	```
625	
626	#### Virtualization
627	
628	Use if you want to use grid container as the scroll element (if you want to use window see window virtualization section). Be sure to set a fixed height on the container; otherwise, virtualization will not work.
629	
630	```tsx
631	import {useRowVirtualizer} from '@gravity-ui/table';
632	
633	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
634	  /* ... */
635	];
636	
637	const data: Person[] = [
638	  /* ... */
639	];
640	
641	const VirtualizationExample = () => {
642	  const table = useTable({
643	    columns,
644	    data,
645	    getRowId: (item) => item.id,
646	  });
647	
648	  const containerRef = React.useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
649	
650	  const rowVirtualizer = useRowVirtualizer({
651	    count: table.getRowModel().rows.length,
652	    estimateSize: () => 20,
653	    overscan: 5,
654	    getScrollElement: () => containerRef.current,
655	  });
656	
657	  return (
658	    <div ref={containerRef} style={{height: '500px', overflow: 'auto'}}>
659	      <Table table={table} rowVirtualizer={rowVirtualizer} />
660	    </div>
661	  );
662	};
663	```
664	
665	For tables that must stay covered during continuous bidirectional scrolling, enable the adaptive
666	direct-DOM mode and use stable semantic keys. The same key must identify a row before and after an
667	immutable reorder or a tree reparent:
668	
669	```tsx
670	import {getColumnAwareRowOverscan} from '@gravity-ui/table';
671	
672	const rows = table.getRowModel().rows;
673	const columnCount = table.getVisibleLeafColumns().length;
674	
675	const getItemKey = React.useCallback(
676	  (index: number) => rows[index]?.id ?? `missing:${index}`,
677	  [rows],
678	);
679	
680	const rowVirtualizer = useRowVirtualizer({
681	  adaptiveFlushSync: true,
682	  count: rows.length,
683	  directDomUpdates: true,
684	  directDomUpdatesMode: 'position',
685	  estimateSize: () => 40,
686	  getItemKey,
687	  getScrollElement: () => containerRef.current,
688	  overscan: getColumnAwareRowOverscan(columnCount),
689	});
690	```
691	
692	`adaptiveFlushSync` keeps a warm mounted range and synchronously fills only an uncovered visible
693	range. `directDomUpdates` lets the virtualizer update row positions and the body size without a
694	React render for every scroll notification. Use `position` for table rows unless transforms are
695	required by the surrounding layout. Keep `getRowId` and `getItemKey` stable, and set `count` from
696	the current flattened row model after expanding, collapsing, reordering, or reparenting rows.
697	An arbitrary custom `rangeExtractor` remains authoritative and disables adaptive window planning.
698	
699	`getColumnAwareRowOverscan(columnCount, options?)` reduces the base row overscan as the number
700	of columns grows. By default, it divides a 240-cell budget by the column count, rounds down,
701	and clamps the result to 4–24 rows. Use `table.getVisibleLeafColumns().length` to exclude hidden
702	columns and include pinned columns. The helper works with both `useRowVirtualizer` and
703	`useWindowRowVirtualizer`; you can still pass an explicit numeric `overscan` instead.
704	
705	Tune the budget and bounds for your cell rendering cost. If your application virtualizes columns,
706	set `renderedColumnLimit` to the maximum number of columns rendered per row, including pinned
707	columns; the helper caps the supplied column count at this value:
708	
709	```tsx
710	const overscan = getColumnAwareRowOverscan(table.getVisibleLeafColumns().length, {
711	  renderedColumnLimit: 16,
712	  cellBudget: 320,
713	  minOverscan: 4,
714	  maxOverscan: 20,
715	});
716	```
717	
718	The result is a base row overscan, not a strict limit on mounted rows or cells. Visible rows are
719	rendered in addition to the overscan, and adaptive scrolling can extend the mounted range.
720	All helper inputs must be non-negative safe integers, and `maxOverscan` must be at least
721	`minOverscan`; invalid values throw a `RangeError`. Zero columns are treated as one for the calculation.
722	
723	`BaseTable.canDeferOffscreenCellContent` is an additional opt-in for very wide adaptive tables.
724	Return `true` only for passive cell content whose delayed mount cannot change geometry, focus,
725	accessibility, or application state. Custom rows, group rows, pinned cells, and interactive or
726	side-effectful content should remain eager.
727	
728	With the default adaptive range extractor, `BaseTable` pins the active dragged row automatically.
729	A custom range extractor is responsible for retaining that row itself. If you use reordering with
730	a non-adaptive virtualizer, keep the same semantic `getItemKey` contract and pass the
731	`rangeExtractor` option:
732	
733	```tsx
734	import {getVirtualRowRangeExtractor} from '@gravity-ui/table';
735	
736	// ...
737	
738	const tableRef = React.useRef<HTMLTableElement>(null);
739	
740	const rowVirtualizer = useRowVirtualizer({
741	  // ...
742	  rangeExtractor: getVirtualRowRangeExtractor(tableRef.current),
743	});
744	
745	return (
746	  <TableWithReordering
747	    ref={tableRef}
748	    table={table}
749	    rowVirtualizer={rowVirtualizer}
750	    onReorder={handleReorder}
751	  />
752	);
753	```
754	
755	#### Window virtualization
756	
757	Use if you want to use window as the scroll element
758	
759	```tsx
760	import {useWindowRowVirtualizer} from '@gravity-ui/table';
761	
762	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
763	  /* ... */
764	];
765	
766	const data: Person[] = [
767	  /* ... */
768	];
769	
770	const WindowVirtualizationExample = () => {
771	  const table = useTable({
772	    columns,
773	    data,
774	    getRowId: (item) => item.id,
775	  });
776	
777	  const bodyRef = React.useRef<HTMLTableSectionElement>(null);
778	
779	  const rowVirtualizer = useWindowRowVirtualizer({
780	    count: table.getRowModel().rows.length,
781	    estimateSize: () => 20,
782	    overscan: 5,
783	    scrollMargin: bodyRef.current?.offsetTop ?? 0,
784	  });
785	
786	  return <Table table={table} rowVirtualizer={rowVirtualizer} bodyRef={bodyRef} />;
787	};
788	```
789	
790	#### Resizing
791	
792	```tsx
793	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
794	  /* ... */
795	];
796	
797	const data: Person[] = [
798	  /* ... */
799	];
800	
801	const ResizingDemo = () => {
802	  const table = useTable({
803	    columns,
804	    data,
805	    enableColumnResizing: true,
806	    columnResizeMode: 'onChange',
807	  });
808	
809	  return <Table table={table} />;
810	};
811	```
812	
813	#### Column settings
814	
815	Set `enableReset` to `true` to show the settings popup's Reset button (hidden by default).
816	It restores column visibility and order from the table's `initialState`. Reset changes
817	the popup draft; press Apply to save it. Without an `initialState`, Reset shows all
818	columns in their definition order.
819	The optional `onSettingsReset` callback receives that restored visibility and column order
820	when Reset is clicked, before the draft is applied.
821	
822	```tsx
823	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
824	  // ...other columns
825	  {
826	    id: 'settings_column_id',
827	    header: ({table}) => <TableSettings table={table} />,
828	    meta: {
829	      hideInSettings: false, // Optional. Allows to hide this column from settings popover
830	      titleInSettings: 'ReactNode', // Optional. Overrides header field for settings popover (if you need different content for header and settings popover)
831	    },
832	  }, // or you can use function getSettingsColumn
833	];
834	
835	const data: Person[] = [
836	  /* ... */
837	];
838	
839	const TableSettingsDemo = () => {
840	  const [columnVisibility, onColumnVisibilityChange] = React.useState<VisibilityState>({
841	    // for outside control and initial state
842	    column_id: false, // for hidding by default
843	  });
844	  const [columnOrder, onColumnOrderChange] = React.useState<string[]>([
845	    /* leaf columns ids */
846	  ]); // for outside control and initial state
847	
848	  // Alternative variant to get state, callbacks, and set on setting apply callbacks - using useTableSettings hook:
849	  // const {state, callbacks} = useTableSettings({initialVisibility: {}, initialOrder: []})
850	
851	  const table = useTable({
852	    columns,
853	    data,
854	    state: {
855	      columnVisibility,
856	      columnOrder,
857	    },
858	    onColumnVisibilityChange,
859	    onColumnOrderChange,
860	  });
861	
862	  return <Table table={table} />;
863	};
864	```
865	
866	Learn more about the table and the column resizing properties in the react-table [docs](https://tanstack.com/table/v8/docs/api/features/column-sizing)
867	
868	## Guides
869	
870	- [Migration Guide: From Table (@gravity-ui/uikit) to Table (@gravity-ui/table)](./guides/migration-from-uikit-table/migration-from-uikit-table.md)
871	- [Руководство по миграции с Table (@gravity-ui/uikit) на Table (@gravity-ui/table)](./guides/migration-from-uikit-table/migration-from-uikit-table-ru.md)
872	
873	## Components
874	
875	- [BaseTable](./components/BaseTable.md) — The unstyled, low-level table renderer — renders a useTable instance as raw <table> markup without Gravity UI styling, for full visual control.
876	
877	## Hooks
878	
879	- [useColumnsAutoSize](./hooks/useColumnsAutoSize.md) — A React hook that automatically calculates column widths based on measured content, supporting primitives and React nodes, accessorKey/accessorFn columns, custom cell renderers, and respect for predefined or user-resized widths.
